Indian Olympic Association (IOA) President P. T. Usha. File | Photo Credit: Shashi Kumar Kashyap
There will be a new president at the helm of a new-look Indian Olympic Association but who it might be remains unclear.
Incumbent P.T. Usha did not turn up on the final day of filing nominations for the upcoming Executive Council elections, effectively marking the end of her innings as the first woman IOA president, even as Tuesday (November 24, 2026) saw more activity at the IOA Bhawan here than it has seen in a long time.
While former Secretary General and Fencing Association of India secretary Rajeev Mehta set the all rolling with his nomination for the top spot on Monday (November 23, 2026), the final hours saw most of the prospective contestants rolling in to file their nominations. Current vice-president and Olympic medalist shooter Gagan Narang has emerged as a frontrunner but archery association secretary and Delhi BJP leader Virender Sachdeva is also in the fray, making it a three-way contest.
Sachdeva, however, has also filed for the male vice-president’s spot, along with boxer Vijender Singh, while Anju Bobby George is being challenged by Bhavneet Handoo of wushu and Suman Kaushik from netball for the female VP post. Former table tennis player Kamlesh Mehta is set to be the next treasurer as the lone candidate.
Senior VP Ajay Patel is seeking another term with Mona Shah (swimming) and netball’s Vagish Pathak challenging him. Sunaina Kumari and Amitabh Sharma are among those fighting to be joint secretaries, along with archer Purnima Mahato and ice hockey’s Harjinder Singh. The nominations also present interesting permutations, with Vijender and Harjinder being proposed by Usha.
With some of the big names from the present EC missing out, including treasurer and weightlifting boss Sahdev Yadav, football chief Kalyan Choubey — who, incidentally, is the proposer for Narang — and shuttler Saina Nehwal, one of the four elected Sportsperson of Outstanding Merit (SOM), the next leadership of the IOA is expected to have a new look leading India’s sporting organisation for the next four years.
Rani Rampal and Yogeshwar Dutt have filed for the SOM quota of EC and are set to be nominated unopposed while Dola Banerjee, Bhupinder Singh Bajwa, R.N. Jayaprakash, Prashant Kushwaha, Vitthal Shirgaonkar, Mona and Suman Kaushik are in the fray for the remaining four EC spots.
Elections are scheduled for December 5 for 13 positions – President, senior vice-president and treasurer (one each), vice-presidents and joint secretaries (two each, one male and female) and six EC members including two from among the Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) elected earlier.
However, with the Sports Ministry and political circles keen on unanimous choices, and the deadline for withdrawing names set for December 2 at 5 pm, the next week is set to see more action in the corridors of power than on the field. It also remains to be seen if Usha presents India’s bid to the IOCs Future Hosts Commission for the 2036 Olympics scheduled on Thursday (December 24, 2026).
